items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol (API name gpt-6.1-sol) at $2 per million input tokens, $0.10 cached input and $10 output. OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra on a coding benchmark at one fifth of the price.
items.why: Rerun your own evals on it and compare cost per task, because price per task now decides which model you ship.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 (API name claude-sonnet-5-5) at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens, with cache reads at $0.20. Anthropic says it is over 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and can cost up to 30% less per task.
items.why: Practice measuring cost per finished task, not only price per token, and use prompt caching to cut your bill.

items.title: OpenAI Agents API with computer use
items.summary: At DevDay OpenAI announced an Agents API with computer use, multi-agent support, tool search and calling, and context compaction on OpenAI-managed infrastructure.
items.why: Build a small agent that uses tools and hands work to a second agent, and know how to test each step.

items.title: MCP Events for plugin automations
items.summary: OpenAI said its plugins now support the MCP Events specification, so a plugin can start an automation when something happens in a connected app. The spec is a community MCP working group draft.
items.why: Learn MCP servers, then read the Events spec so your tools can trigger agents, not only answer them.

items.title: Decisions API (limited preview)
items.summary: OpenAI announced a Decisions API that takes text or images and returns one answer from a fixed list, aimed at classification, routing and agent direction. It is in limited preview, with broad release planned within days.
items.why: Practice using small fixed-answer routing steps inside agents, and compare them with a normal model call in your evals.
